open_points.subject: data-provider correspondence models
open_points.text: `models`: the row models of its tables and the enumerations their cells name.
open_points.question: Which row models and cell enumerations back the four new tables, and what are the exact members of each cell enumeration? No such models or enumerations are defined in M01–M28 or in the `models` module section.
options: Add explicit row models and cell enumerations to `models`
Use existing enumerations wherever possible and define only the missing conclusion/body taxonomies
Represent some cells as non-enumeration values, contradicting the statement that cells name members
open_points.default_guess: Use existing NodeExecutionStatus, WaitingReason, RunStatus and HTTPMethod enums as keys, and add explicit enums for node conclusions, conclusion effects and body presence.

open_points.subject: EXECUTION_STATUS_CONCLUSIONS
open_points.text: the conclusion each NodeExecution status gives (A13 rules 5 and 7)
open_points.question: What table cell applies to `outcome_unknown`, whose conclusion is not determined by its NodeExecution status alone but changes according to the associated EffectAttempt (`unknown`, resolved `applied` with or without outputs, or resolved `not_applied`)?
options: Map it to a member meaning that `effects.operation_element_conclusion` must consult the EffectAttempt
Make the table depend on both NodeExecution status and EffectAttempt state
Map it permanently to waiting, which conflicts with A11 rule 3 after resolution
open_points.default_guess: Map `outcome_unknown` to a special deferred conclusion that requires consulting the EffectAttempt and binding outputs.

open_points.subject: NODE_CONCLUSION_EFFECTS
open_points.text: what each node conclusion means for the run and for its dependants (A13 rules 5 and 7)
open_points.question: What is the closed set of node conclusions, and what exact columns and cell mappings express their separate effects on run completion and dependant propagation, including `skipped_by_guard`, `upstream_failed`, `refused_by_owner`, `applied_outputs_unknown`, waits and the mapped-list failure that has no NodeExecution?
options: One row per conclusion with separate run-effect and dependant-effect enum cells
Two independent correspondence tables, one for run effects and one for dependant effects
Reuse NodeExecution statuses as conclusions and handle derived cases procedurally outside the table
open_points.default_guess: Define a closed NodeConclusion taxonomy and a row with separate run-effect and dependant-effect cells, including all derived conclusions.

open_points.subject: HTTP_METHOD_BODIES
open_points.text: whether an HTTP method carries a body (A09 rule 2) — is a correspondence over that taxonomy ... whose cells name members
open_points.question: Is `HTTP_METHOD_BODIES` a boolean mapping, or which enumeration supplies the cell members for body/no-body? The stated fact is boolean, but the table rule requires cells to name enumeration members and no body-presence enumeration is defined.
options: A new enumeration such as `no_body` and `body`
A request-body-mode enumeration distinguishing no body, JSON and multipart
open_points.default_guess: Use a two-member body-presence enumeration, mapping GET and DELETE to no body and POST, PUT and PATCH to body.
